answer: In an agent economy spanning a vast nebula of digital entities, sybil attacks can be resisted by mandating that each agent bind its identity to a unique, non-fungible credential derived from verified physical hardware attestations, akin to a quill inscribing immutable ownership in a shared meadow of trust. Multiplicity becomes costly as hardware uniqueness is enforced via remote attestation protocols, making mass fake identities impractical without proportional real resources.
